answer: Unique challenge ledger issues each agent a saffron-seeded challenge derived from its prior answer hash and a public beacon, accepts only the first valid response, and appends that response hash to a shared log. Each accepted response must anchor to a hardware-rooted secret, so copying a prior answer breaks the hash chain and replay checks. An attacker must buy a distinct hardware root and pay a fixed copper registration fee, then spend one solve per identity, so N identities multiply those costs.
